a: The power to participate in the financial and operating policy decisions of an investee, without control or joint control of those policies.

q: What does a holding of 20% or more of the voting power presume?
a: Significant influence, unless it can be clearly shown not to exist. Under 20% is presumed not to give it, unless shown otherwise.
source: ST p.385 (IAS 28 para. 5 as quoted); Kit fp.170

q: Name four usual signs of significant influence.
a: Board representation; taking part in policy-making; material transactions with the investee; exchange of managerial staff; providing essential technical information (any four).

q: How is an associate measured under the equity method?
a: At cost, adjusted for the investor's share of the post-acquisition change in the associate's net assets. It is not the fair value of the shares.

q: Is cash in transit from an associate adjusted, as for a subsidiary?
a: No. An associate is not consolidated line by line, so no cash-in-transit adjustment is made.

q: How much unrealised profit on sales to an associate is eliminated, and against what?
a: Only the investor's share, against the investment in associate.
When decisions about the relevant activities need the unanimous consent of the parties sharing control (contractually agreed sharing of control).

q: Joint operation vs joint venture: what is the test?
a: Joint operation: parties have direct rights to assets and obligations for liabilities. Joint venture: parties have rights to the net assets of the arrangement.

q: How does a party account for a joint operation, and for a joint venture?
a: Joint operation: recognise its own share of each asset, liability, revenue and expense. Joint venture: equity method, one investment line.
